title: Bounded computation of a Boolean disjunction
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c_j$ be a configuration on a common input for each $0\le j\le N$, and let $a$ be a Boolean-valued function on the natural numbers. Suppose $c_N$ is halted with output the one-bit word $[\mathrm{false}]$. For every $j<N$, assume there is a time $t\le B$ such that, if $a(j)$ is true, the run from $c_j$ is halted at time $t$ with output $[\mathrm{true}]$; if $a(j)$ is false, the run from $c_j$ at time $t$ equals $c_{j+1}$. Then there is a time $t\le NB$ at which the run from $c_0$ is halted and has output the one-bit word whose value is true exactly when $a(j)$ is true for some $j<N$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
The configurations c_j are indexed by natural numbers and share a common input
a maps natural numbers to Booleans
N and B are natural numbers
For every j<N, some t≤B satisfies the specified conditional run outcome
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c_0, \dots, c_N$
be configurations of $M$ on a common input with $c_N$ halted with output the single bit
$\mathrm{false}$, and let $a$ be a Boolean predicate on round indices. Assume for each
$j < N$ that within $B$ steps the machine either halts from $c_j$ with output the single
bit $\mathrm{true}$ (when $a(j)$ holds) or reaches $c_{j+1}$ (when $a(j)$ fails). Then
from $c_0$ the machine halts within $N \cdot B$ steps with output the single bit
recording whether $a(j)$ holds for some $j < N$.
